incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/chat/streaming — paging oncall (sev: high) :rotating_light:

marisol: Paging team — p99 across prod crossed 1.2s at ~1739509900, p95 ~450ms. Streaming tail stalls reported by multiple customers. Not sure if it's template expansion or tokenizer. Seeing big increase in preproc CPU. Anyone oncall?

raj: I'm oncall. joining now. What svc/route is hot?

marisol: Mostly /v1/chat/streaming with JSON-mode and templates. Affected routes: chat-tooling (high qps), customer-prod-42. Logs show a surge in `prompt_builder` durations and `tokenizer.expand()` times.

samir: Confirming. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/streams/streaming-latency ?orgId=1 (stacked view) — look at `ingress->preproc->runtime` flame. There's a cluster of slow tail requests with `template_render_ms` spiking to 800ms.

eva: Are we seeing any deploys in the last ~30m?

marisol: No code deploys in last hour (ci-bot shows nothing). But autoscaling bumped a subset of dedicated workers ~20m ago. Not sure that explains per-request tails.

raj: Pulling recent traces. `trace_id=ab12..` shows long time in `TemplateAssembler.render` then `TokenizationService.tokenize`. Attaching snippet:

```
TemplateAssembler.render  820ms
  -> ToolSchema.serialize  240ms
  -> TemplateEngine.expand  560ms
TokenizationService.tokenize  410ms
  -> tokeniser::vocab_lookup  200ms
  -> tokeniser::match_long_tokens  210ms
```

marisol: That `ToolSchema.serialize` is new-ish since we rolled in tool schema validation changes last week. Could be pathological shapes causing combinatorial expansion.

samir: Runbook suggests toggling `JSON_MODE` to false for affected routes as a mitigation (reduces schema assembly). Can we patch route-level config?

kelly: I can flip route config in the console for chat-tooling and customer-prod-42 to disable JSON-mode and reduce template expansion. Quick question: will this change impact downstream clients expecting structured output? Need to coordinate.

marisol: Yes, it will change output shape. But we only flip for a fraction of traffic (10% canary -> 100% if stable). Prioritize availability over structure for now.

raj: Meanwhile, adding temporary prefix caching for those routes to cut down repeated template work. `curl -X POST https://console/api/cache/rules -d '{"route":"/v1/chat/streaming","prefix":true,"ttl":30}'`

samir: Throttling ingest to 80% for the customer-prod-42 tenant to reduce queuing. Using quota service: `quotactl set tenant/customer-prod-42 rate 0.8`

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff required in 2 hours. Add postmortem tag if escalated.

eva: Results from the config flips: after toggling JSON_MODE for chat-tooling canary (10% at 1739510200) p99 dropped from 1.2s to 420ms on canary. p95 stable at ~380ms. Streaming stalls for canary requests gone.

marisol: Good. Roll canary to 50% now and keep monitoring. If 50% stable for 10m, roll to 100%.

kelly: Rolling to 50% at 1739510600. Observability: pushing new dashboards for template_render_ms and tokenizer_ms per-tenant.

samir: Also seeing one long-running job on node gpu-prod-07: `preproc_worker` stuck at 98% CPU doing `schema.serialize` with repeated recursion. Killing and restarting worker freed backlog. Might be memory leak in the schema serializer for arrays > 500 elements. Opening an issue.

raj: Live mitigation summary so far:
- disabled JSON_MODE (canary -> 10% -> 50%) for affected routes
- applied prefix caching rule for streaming route (ttl=30s)
- throttled tenant customer-prod-42 to 80%
- restarted stuck preproc worker on gpu-prod-07

marisol: Customer impact: Estimated 12% of streaming requests hit tail stalls during window (~1739509200-1739510000). Affected customers reported degraded interactive latency and a few streaming timeouts. No data loss. Ticketing: CS has initial notes.

kelly: Alerting: create follow-up alert to catch `template_render_ms > 400ms` and `tokenizer_ms > 250ms` per-tenant. Add a runbook link.

samir: Investigating root cause: suspect combinatorial expansion when tool schemas include large optional arrays + deep nested templates. JSON-mode triggers a full schema serialization pass for assembly. We need to short-circuit serialization for streaming path or add early size guards.

marisol: Agreed. For now mitigation is config-level. For long-term: patch serializer to bail if array depth > 3 or total elements > 200, and add telemetry. Also consider caching serialized tool schema at model-serving level.

raj: I'll own the patch. Creating GH issue: `redwood/preproc#4821` with stack traces and sample payloads. Will prototype a guard and unit test.

kelly: Ops tasks: update post-incident notes, notify affected customers with mitigation timeline, and schedule an RFC for serializer changes.

incident-bot: REMINDER: Attach `sev=high` postmortem if any SLOs breached. Current SLO: streaming p99 < 500ms. We exceeded that briefly.

marisol: Assigning follow-ups:
- raj -> code fix + PR by EOD + test (preproc serializer short-circuit)
- samir -> reproduce case and add unit/integration tests with large tool schemas
- kelly -> customer comms and alerting rules + runbook links
- marisol -> postmortem draft (include timeline and mitigation steps)

eva: Handoff: I'm taking the next shift for monitoring and will coordinate with raj for the PR review. If anything regresses, page me.

samir: Quick note for oncall: if we see p99 re-spike after config roll, run `diag-preproc --slow -n 50 --filter tenant=customer-prod-42` and capture `template_render_ms` histogram.

marisol: Closing the live mitigation. Keeping thread open for postmortem updates. Thanks everyone. :heart:

kelly: Adding final notes — sequence numbers, logs, and traced requests saved under incident-1739509999 in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1739509999/trace.tar.gz

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved -> status: mitigated. Marking for postmortem review.

marisol: Postmortem owners, please add remediation ETA and link to PRs. We'll review on Monday triage.
